svg.title: Isolation levels in PostgreSQL: Read Committed takes a new snapshot per statement, so read-then-write code can lose updates; Repeatable Read keeps one snapshot and raises a serialisation error on a conflicting update but still allows write skew; Serializable (SSI) also detects the cycles behind write skew. InnoDB’s Repeatable Read differs: its updates see the latest rows, so lost updates remain possible there.
